entry.label: Distributed ethnography
entry.description: Participative research approach in which many people contribute situated observations or micro-narratives and interpret their own material, reducing sole dependence on an external analyst's coding scheme.
entry.canonical_definition: Participative research approach in which many people contribute situated observations or micro-narratives and interpret their own material, reducing sole dependence on an external analyst's coding scheme.

profile.title: Distributed ethnography
profile.canonical_definition: Participative research approach in which many people contribute situated observations or micro-narratives and interpret their own material, reducing sole dependence on an external analyst's coding scheme.
profile.summary: Distributed ethnography spreads observation and interpretation across many situated participants rather than reserving both to a small external research team.
profile.why_it_matters: It can increase contextual variety and reduce some analyst-imposed categories, while raising new sampling, ethics, inclusion and interpretation questions.
key_distinctions: participant interpretation vs absence of research design
open_checks: compare with conventional and digital ethnography
profile.editorial_note: Developed from public primary, institutional, publisher and project sources. First-party source roles and independent evidential limits are stated explicitly.
